 Key Points
 The Social Security Administration set 2027 maximum taxable earnings at $192,300, up $7,800 from $184,500 in 2026.
 Workers earning $192,300 or more will pay up to $11,922.60 in Social Security tax, $483.60 more than in 2026.
 The 6.2% rate is unchanged, and self-employed workers pay both halves , up to $23,845.20.
 Social Security’s maximum taxable earnings will rise to $192,300 in 2027, the Social Security Administration announced . That’s an increase of $7,800, or about 4.2%, from the 2026 cap of $184,500. 
 The update came out alongside the 3.6% Social Security COLA for 2027 , the largest benefit increase since 2023.
 The tax rate itself isn’t changing. Employees pay 6.2% of covered wages up to the cap, and employers pay a matching 6.2%. Under the SSA’s contribution and benefit base table , anyone earning $192,300 or more will pay $11,922.60 in 2027, up from $11,439. The 1.45% Medicare tax still applies to every dollar of pay.
 Social Security Tax Limits For 2027 Item 2026 2027 
 Maximum Taxable Earnings $184,500 $192,300 
 Employee Tax Rate 6.2% 6.2% 
 Maximum Employee Tax $11,439 $11,922.60 
 Maximum Self-Employed Tax $22,878 $23,845.20 
 Medicare Tax Earnings Cap None None 
 Earnings For One Credit $1,890 $1,970 
 Earnings For Four Credits $7,560 $7,880 
 Maximum Monthly Benefit At Full Retirement Age $4,152 $4,188 
 Source: Social Security Administration. The College Investor.

 Why It Matters
 The SSA’s formal name for this number is the contribution and benefit base, because it sets two limits at once. It caps the pay that owes Social Security tax, and that same figure limits the earnings counted toward your future benefit. A worker who earns $250,000 in 2027 gets credit for only $192,300 on their Social Security record. 
 Most workers won’t see any change from the new cap. Roughly 6% of covered workers earn above the taxable maximum in a given year, according to SSA research on taxable maximum earners . The agency projects almost 20% of current and future workers will cross it in at least one year. 
 For everyone else, the bigger 2027 change is the inflation update to the 2027 federal tax brackets .
 How Much Social Security Tax Will You Pay In 2027?
 You’ll pay 6.2% of covered wages up to $192,300, so the most any employee owes in 2027 is $11,922.60 if you make or exceed the limit. Workers earning under $184,500 pay the same Social Security tax on the same salary as in 2026. Only pay between $184,500 and $192,300 is newly taxed, which caps the increase at $483.60. 
 You can see how payroll taxes stack up with income tax in our federal income tax calculator .
 Employee Social Security Tax By Salary In 2027 Salary 2026 Tax 2027 Tax Change 
 $75,000 $4,650 $4,650 No change 
 $150,000 $9,300 $9,300 No change 
 $184,500 $11,439 $11,439 No change 
 $192,300 $11,439 $11,922.60 +$483.60 
 $250,000 $11,439 $11,922.60 +$483.60 
 Source: Social Security Administration. The College Investor. 
 High earners also see bigger paychecks late in the year. A worker earning $250,000 and paid every two weeks reaches $192,300 on the 20th paycheck of 2027. Social Security withholding stops for the last six checks, so each one keeps about $596 more. 
 Employers keep withholding the 1.45% Medicare tax , plus the 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax on wages above $200,000.
 What If You’re Self-Employed Or Work Two Jobs?
 Self-employed workers pay both halves, so the Social Security portion of self-employment tax is 12.4% on net earnings up to $192,300. That puts the 2027 maximum at $23,845.20, up $967.20 from 2026. The IRS applies self-employment tax to 92.35% of net earnings. That means you’d need about $208,230 in net profit to reach the cap.
 If you have a W-2 job and a side business, your wages count toward the cap first. Schedule SE subtracts those wages, so side income owes the 12.4% only on the room left under $192,300. 
 Freelancers near the cap should rerun their quarterly side hustle tax payments for 2027, since the higher base can add up to $967.20.
 Workers with two employers can overpay. Each employer withholds Social Security tax on its own wages up to $192,300, so combined withholding can top $11,922.60. A midyear job switch can trigger it, since a new employer starts withholding from zero no matter what’s on your Form W-4 . You get the excess back as a credit on your federal return.
 What Does The 2027 Change Mean For Students And New Workers?
 The cap won’t touch most students or new graduates, but a companion number will. One Social Security credit takes $1,970 of covered earnings in 2027, and $7,880 earns the maximum four credits for the year. You need 40 credits to qualify for retirement benefits , which takes at least 10 years of work. A summer job or one of the best side hustles for college students can clear $7,880 in a year.
 Some campus jobs don’t count toward those credits. Wages covered by the IRS student FICA exception skip Social Security tax, so they don’t earn credits. Self-employed students do earn credits, since net side hustle income of $400 or more owes self-employment tax.
 How This Connects
 The higher wage base lands next to two other 2027 updates we’ve covered. Retirees get a 3.6% COLA starting in January , and the IRS raised the 2027 tax brackets about 3.2% for inflation. The wage base rose faster, at 4.2%, because it tracks the national average wage from 2024 to 2025 rather than consumer prices.
 Student loan borrowers on income-driven repayment plans should know which taxes touch their payment. For W-2 workers, Social Security tax doesn’t lower adjusted gross income, so it doesn’t lower an IDR payment. A traditional 401k contribution does lower AGI, though it doesn’t reduce Social Security tax, as our income tax calculator notes . 
 What’s Next
 The $192,300 cap applies to wages paid starting January 1, 2027. High earners should check their late-2027 pay stubs, and job switchers should compare box 4 on every W-2 when they file in early 2028. 
 The SSA will set the 2028 cap in October 2027 using 2026 national wage data. Watch for the IRS’s 2027 retirement plan limits too, which we track on our 401k contribution limits page .
